title: The most expensive hyphen in history
caption:
NASA's first Venus probe was blown up by its own safety officer less than five minutes after launch. Because of one missing line. ✏️
The bar over a symbol meant 'use the smoothed, averaged speed': without it the guidance program chased every random jitter and steered the rocket off course.
Who is more to blame: the person who wrote the formula or the people who never checked it?
first_comment: One missing bar, $18.5 million. Every code reviewer just felt a chill 🥶 Typo or process failure?
sources: NASA NSSDCA, 'Mariner 1': launched 22 July 1962, destroyed by the range safety officer 293 seconds after launch when it veered off course; the cause was an error in the guidance equations (a missing overbar, meaning smoothed velocity) combined with a loss of the guidance radar signal; cost about $18.5 million
Arthur C. Clarke, 'The Promise of Space' (1968): 'the most expensive hyphen in history'
